title: Tell which date order a document uses
description: Say whether a document writes the day or the month first, using a date that makes it obvious.
oneStarDescription: Find a numeric date on a document.
twoStarDescription: Use a number greater than 12, or the document's own words, to say which order it uses.
threeStarDescription: Find or imagine a date such as 04/05 and say you cannot tell the order from that date alone.

title: Test a bicycle brake
description: Squeeze a brake and say whether the wheel stops, without adjusting a cable.
oneStarDescription: With the bike still, lift the wheel and spin it.
twoStarDescription: Squeeze the lever and say whether the wheel stops promptly.
threeStarDescription: If it does not stop the wheel, say you will not ride it, and do not adjust the cable in this skill.

title: Test a chair before you use it as a step
description: Decide not to stand on a chair that rocks, and choose a safer way to reach.
oneStarDescription: Rock the chair on the floor and say whether all feet sit.
twoStarDescription: If it rocks or is soft, say you will not stand on it.
threeStarDescription: Ask for a proper step, leave the object, or wait, and say which you chose.

title: Test a form with a person
description: Watch one person fill a form you made or chose, and fix one confusion.
oneStarDescription: Give them the form and do not explain the fields while they try.
twoStarDescription: Write the field where they stop or ask a question.
threeStarDescription: Rewrite the label of that field and say what was unclear.

title: Test which cloth soaks water
description: Compare two cloths by how they take up a spoon of water.
oneStarDescription: Put the same small amount of water on two cloths.
twoStarDescription: Say which cloth spread or held the water more, and show it.
threeStarDescription: Say which you would put under a wet cup, and one reason the test might not match a real spill.

title: Test what floats
description: Test small objects in water and sort them by whether they float.
oneStarDescription: Place small objects in a bowl of water and sort them into floats and sinks.
twoStarDescription: Change the shape of one material, such as a flat sheet and a boat, and say what changed.
threeStarDescription: Write one rule you will not claim, because you tested only these objects.

title: Tighten a screw you can see
description: Tighten one visible screw on furniture until it sits, and stop if it spins.
oneStarDescription: Choose a driver that fits the screw head.
twoStarDescription: Turn it until it is snug, and show that the part sits closer.
threeStarDescription: If the screw spins or the hole is stripped, stop and say so.

title: Time a pendulum
description: Time a swinging weight and see what happens when you change the length.
oneStarDescription: Time a counted run of swings of the same pendulum and write the time.
twoStarDescription: Change only the length, time the same count, and say which was slower.
threeStarDescription: Say one thing you did not change, such as the weight, so you do not claim it was tested.

title: Trace a number to its source
description: Take a number from a text and find the source it cites, or say the source is missing.
oneStarDescription: Point to a number and the sentence that uses it.
twoStarDescription: Find the citation, link, or table the sentence points to, or write that there is none.
threeStarDescription: If you found the source, say whether the number matches, or that you could not open it.

title: Trace a shape and cut it out
description: Trace a shape and cut it out so the line is still visible or just gone, as you intended.
oneStarDescription: Trace a shape you are allowed to copy onto paper.
twoStarDescription: Cut along the line you traced, keeping the shape in one piece.
threeStarDescription: Lay the cut on the original and say where you left the line.

title: Track a shadow
description: Mark a shadow twice and say how it moved.
oneStarDescription: Mark the tip of a shadow and the time.
twoStarDescription: Mark it later and say which way the tip moved.
threeStarDescription: Say that this does not give a clock or a compass bearing by itself, and why.

title: Turn a table into a sentence
description: Write one sentence a table supports, and one it does not.
oneStarDescription: Say what the columns or rows are.
twoStarDescription: Write one sentence and point to the cells it uses.
threeStarDescription: Write a sentence a reader might think the table says, and show that the cells do not say it.

title: Unpack an archive and find the file
description: Open a compressed archive and find the file you were sent, without running a program you did not expect.
oneStarDescription: Open a zip or similar archive you were expecting.
twoStarDescription: Find the named file inside and open that file.
threeStarDescription: If you see a program you were not told about, do not run it, and say so.

title: Use a dot vote
description: Let a group mark preferences with a limited number of dots, then read the result.
oneStarDescription: Say how many dots each person gets and that a dot is a preference, not a decision by itself.
twoStarDescription: Count the dots in front of the group.
threeStarDescription: Say what the dots did not settle, such as who will do the work.

title: Use guide words in a dictionary
description: Use the guide words on a dictionary page to find a word.
oneStarDescription: Read the two guide words on a page and say which words would belong there.
twoStarDescription: Open the right page for a word you chose and point to the entry.
threeStarDescription: If the word is not there, say whether to go forward or back, and find it.

title: Wait without filling the silence
description: Leave a silence so the other person can speak, instead of jumping in.
oneStarDescription: After they stop, wait before you speak.
twoStarDescription: If they continue, do not talk over the new sentence.
threeStarDescription: If they do not continue, ask whether they want a question or quiet, and follow the answer.

title: Warm up your voice
description: Do a short gentle voice warm-up and stop if anything hurts.
oneStarDescription: Hum or speak a simple pattern quietly for a short time.
twoStarDescription: Repeat a little louder and say whether it feels easy.
threeStarDescription: Name the signal that would stop you, such as pain or a tickle, and stop if it appears.

title: Watch an insect on a flower
description: Watch one insect visit a flower and write what it did.
oneStarDescription: Watch one insect for a short time and write what it did on the flower.
twoStarDescription: Describe the flower well enough to find a similar one, without requiring a species name.
threeStarDescription: Write one thing you did not see, such as where the insect went next.

title: Weave a paper mat
description: Weave paper strips into a mat that holds when you pick it up.
oneStarDescription: Lay strips one way and fix the ends so they stay parallel.
twoStarDescription: Weave the other strips over and under, alternating the next row.
threeStarDescription: Fold or tape the edge so a strip does not fall out when you lift the mat.

title: Write a content note
description: Write a short note that tells a reader what difficult thing is ahead, without describing it at length.
oneStarDescription: Write the topic in a few words.
twoStarDescription: Put the note before the material, where the reader can see it first.
threeStarDescription: Remove a sentence that retells the difficult part, and leave the short note.

title: Write a correction
description: Correct something you said or wrote, in the same place the mistake went.
oneStarDescription: Point to the sentence that was wrong and say what was wrong.
twoStarDescription: Write the correction where the original readers can see it.
threeStarDescription: Keep the old line visible or marked, so the change can be seen.

title: Write a factual note to a local service
description: Write to a library, council, or similar service about a fact you saw, and ask one question.
oneStarDescription: Write what you saw, where, and when.
twoStarDescription: Add one question that the fact makes relevant.
threeStarDescription: Remove a sentence that insults or that asks for something you cannot justify, and send or save the note.

title: Write an agenda item in one line
description: Write one agenda item so the group knows the outcome you want.
oneStarDescription: Write the topic in a few words.
twoStarDescription: Add the outcome, such as a decision, a list, or an update.
threeStarDescription: Add a time you will stop, and say what happens if you do not finish.

title: Label a shared moving box
description: Label a shared box with the room and one fragile fact.
oneStarDescription: Write the room the box belongs to.
twoStarDescription: Add one handling note you mean, such as heavy or this way up, only if it is true.
threeStarDescription: Put the box in that room, or correct the label if the room was wrong.

title: Write a plant-care note for someone else
description: Write how to care for one plant while you are away, including when not to water.
oneStarDescription: Write how you decide whether the soil is dry.
twoStarDescription: Write what they should not do, such as watering every day regardless.
threeStarDescription: Write how they should tell you if the plant wilts.

title: Write alt text you can check
description: Write alternative text that matches the image and leaves out a guess.
oneStarDescription: Write one sentence of alt text that names the subject.
twoStarDescription: Remove any claim about why the person is there or how they feel, unless the image states it.
threeStarDescription: Read the alt text to someone who is not looking, then show the image and fix one miss.

title: Write the step-free note on an invitation
description: Add a step-free arrival note to an invitation, or say you do not know it yet.
oneStarDescription: Find the step-free entrance from the venue, or write that you do not know it.
twoStarDescription: Put that sentence on the invitation if you know it.
threeStarDescription: Add a way for a guest to ask, if the note is missing or incomplete.

title: Write what you know about an old photo
description: Write what you know about an old photo, separate from what you suppose.
oneStarDescription: Write only facts someone told you or that are written on the photo.
twoStarDescription: If you add a guess, mark it as a guess.
threeStarDescription: Ask the person who keeps the photo to confirm one line, and correct it.

title: Agree a photo rule
description: Say what may be photographed before people arrive, and where that rule is written.
oneStarDescription: Write what is fine to photograph and what is not.
twoStarDescription: Place it where people see it as they enter.
threeStarDescription: Point to one moment where you followed it or asked.

title: Answer as the character
description: Answer three questions in a character's voice without adding a new power.
oneStarDescription: Write what the character can know.
twoStarDescription: Answer three questions inside those limits.
threeStarDescription: Refuse one question the character could not answer, and say why.

title: Arrange tools in the order you use them
description: Lay out the tools for a small task in the order you will pick them up.
oneStarDescription: Write the order of tools before you lay them out.
twoStarDescription: Place them in that order.
threeStarDescription: Do the task and say where the order failed.

title: Ask before you move their object
description: Ask before you move an object that belongs to the person you are helping.
oneStarDescription: Point to the object and say what you want to do.
twoStarDescription: Wait for a yes, or leave it.
threeStarDescription: If you moved it, put it back where they asked.

title: Ask a closed question, then an open one
description: Ask one yes-or-no question, then one question that needs a sentence.
oneStarDescription: Ask one question that can be answered yes or no.
twoStarDescription: Ask one question that needs more than yes or no.
threeStarDescription: Write both answers and say which one you will act on.

title: Ask someone to name your mark
description: Draw a simple mark and write the word another person uses for it.
oneStarDescription: Draw a mark with no letters on it.
twoStarDescription: Show it and write the word they use.
threeStarDescription: Change the mark if their word was not the one you wanted, and test once more.

title: Ask what a plaque does not say
description: Read a plaque and write one question it does not answer.
oneStarDescription: Summarize what it does say in one sentence.
twoStarDescription: Write one question a reader still has.
threeStarDescription: Say why that question changes how you use the plaque.

title: Ask what they expect
description: Ask what the learner thinks will happen, then show the result.
oneStarDescription: Write their expectation before you demonstrate.
twoStarDescription: Do the ordinary action and show what happened.
threeStarDescription: Ask them what differed from their guess.

title: Ask what they want from you
description: Ask whether they want a listener, a suggestion, or help, before you offer a fix.
oneStarDescription: Ask which of those they want.
twoStarDescription: Wait for the answer before you advise.
threeStarDescription: Do the job they named, or say you cannot.

title: Ask where the eye went
description: Place a title and ask someone where they looked first.
oneStarDescription: Put the title at the start of the path you intend.
twoStarDescription: Ask one person where they looked first, before you explain.
threeStarDescription: If they started elsewhere, move the title and ask again.

title: Bend two straw shapes
description: Bend drinking straws into two shapes and say which held a light book longer.
oneStarDescription: Make two different shapes from the same number of straws.
twoStarDescription: Rest the same light book on each and say which held.
threeStarDescription: Change one joint on the weaker shape and test again.

title: Bind a cord end
description: Bind the end of a cord so it does not fray, then tug the binding.
oneStarDescription: Wrap the end so the strands are covered.
twoStarDescription: Tug the binding and say whether it slipped.
threeStarDescription: If it slips, wrap it again and tug once more.
